text:
**Hi everyone! **

I am writing today with so much joy and a full heart to share some very special news: **Yesterday, I finally received my Israeli citizenship!** After a long legal battle alongside my lawyer against the Ministry of the Interior, I can finally say we did it.

I wanted to share my experience because I know many of you here are going through your own processes. My husband and I are Argentine; we met in 2000 and got married in 2005. He is Jewish, as is his entire family. In 2021, we started the Aliyah process together with my father-in-law, who had a very unique history: he had made Aliyah at around 16 and fought in the war, but at 22 he returned to Argentina, where he started his family. Unfortunately, he never registered his children at the consulate.

Our file was accepted by the Sojnut, but a few months later, my father-in-law passed away. That’s when the labyrinth began: between status changes and consular delays, the Misrad Hapnim decided to declare my husband an Israeli citizen by birth. This left me out of the Aliyah process, forcing me to enter Israel as a foreign spouse.

It was an incredibly tough process. I arrived on a B2 visa and had to face endless interviews to prove that my 17 years of marriage and our 3 children were not part of some "plan" to get citizenship 20 years later. Imagine what it was like gathering paperwork from an entire lifetime! My own children had citizenship through the Law of Return, but I remained a foreigner in the eyes of the State.

After a legal battle where the judge—though empathetic—applied the letter of the law, we didn't give up. Thanks to the persistence of our lawyer and several legal notices, we managed to get Misrad Hapnim to accept an exception. After going through interviews that, honestly, were frustrating and degrading, yesterday I finally obtained my citizenship.

Today, I feel an immense sense of pride in saying that **I am an Israeli citizen**. This is a dream our family has had for a very long time. My case was complex and atypical, and having legal counsel was key to not giving up.

To everyone just starting out or halfway through the journey: **do not lose hope.** Everything comes in time, even if the road is winding.

Finally, I want to deeply thank this Facebook group. You provided me with valuable information from the moment my situation changed, and there was always someone ready to answer my questions.

**Thank you all so much, and stay strong in your processes!** 🇮🇱✨
